title: Stationary-start cover-time lower bound
formal: Does every irreducible reversible discrete-time Markov chain on \(n\ge2\) states satisfy \(\mathbb E_{\pi}C\ge(n-1)H_{n-1}\), where the initial state has stationary distribution \(\pi\), \(C\) counts transitions until every state has been visited, and \(H_j=\sum_{i=1}^{j}1/i\)?

import_provenance.original_title: The exact minimum stationary-start cover time
import_provenance.original_statement: Does every irreducible discrete-time reversible Markov chain on n states satisfy Eπ[C]≥(n−1)H_{n−1}, where the walk starts in stationarity and C is the time to visit all states? This exact bound would strengthen the extremal cover-time line in which Feige established the asymptotic n log n lower bound for unweighted graphs.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial extension of Feige’s extremal cover-time work; the exact reversible-chain conjecture is stated by Aldous and Fill.
